rationale: Confirmed source-level unreferenced attachment keys, downgraded from candidate P2 to P3. Original bytes commit in a standalone transaction before snapshot CAS; every failed retry chooses a new UUID key and the catch neither cleans nor reuses it. A stale repository revision is a concrete failure trigger. Snapshot integrity remains protected. Physical storage duplication, quota exhaustion, and an outage were not measured, so those consequences are not confirmed. Distinct from intentional retention on deletion or the documented server upload-before-snapshot tradeoff.

rationale: Confirmed by React state and mutation flow. The editor retains opening form state but receives updated visit props. rationale: Retain as targeted transport hardening. FoundationNetworking Gemini and shared voice transport collect Data before enforcing their decode caps, while the Apple Gemini path streams with a bound. The code and comments disclose this distinction. A fixed provider or proxy returning too much data can exceed the nominal cap in memory, but no oversized transport run, process failure or arbitrary-destination exploit was demonstrated.

rationale: Retain as a deployment-hardening suggestion and lower its priority from P2 to P3. File receipts are deliberately separate from PostgreSQL snapshots; the frozen server README explicitly requires persistent storage and preservation across redeploys. Losing that storage can lose duplicate-call protection if an external client later resubmits the old request ID, but neither current UI resubmits an existing request. Ephemeral Docker/Tiger deployment was unfinished and is not evidence of a delivered-path defect. Requiring an absolute directory alone would not prove persistence.
